title: A CNN search exposes a real false-positive ceiling and supports validation of TOI-6662 b
summary: Juan Francisco Pagés Navarrete reports a convolutional neural network pipeline for ultra-short-period planet candidates in TESS photometry. In the first arXiv version, replacing synthetic negative examples with real false positives reduced the reported AUC from 0.97 to 0.50; the author identified a blend-related ceiling and retrained using real false positives. The work also applies candidate prioritization and follow-up to statistically validate TOI-6662 b. The validated planet is a specific astronomy result, while the small candidate sample and selection process limit generalization of the benchmark findings.
ai_technology: Convolutional neural network for TESS transit candidate detection

evidence.tested: The v1 compares a CNN against synthetic and real false positives, then uses candidate ranking and statistical follow-up evidence in a specific TOI-6662 b validation. This external/independent confirmation occurred within the same study rather than an independent later research-team follow-up.
evidence.unknown: A small, selected sample limits generalization; statistical validation is not equivalent to a mass measurement, and the CNN is a candidate-prioritization tool.
evidence.ai_role: A convolutional neural network ranks TESS transit candidates; the candidate TOI-6662 b was statistically validated using follow-up and other evidence.

source_review.scope: Primary source full text reviewed for title, authorship, Methods, Results, version date and stated limitations.
